_doc: Lineage origin derivation vectors. Shared fixture: read by
`txid` is written big-endian, the way RPC and explorers display it. The
bytes fed to SHA256 are its REVERSE, followed by n little-endian. A port
that skips the reversal, or writes n big-endian, stays self-consistent
and still disagrees with consensus -- which is what these vectors catch.
A mint's origin is derived from the outpoint being SPENT (the mint
output's own location on chain), at the moment of its first spend. See
the 'lineage identity and merging' section of uap_mint_tests.cpp.

comment: same txid, index 1 -- must differ from the above, or two mints in one transaction collide
asymmetric txid: catches a port that hashes the display bytes without reversing
the byte-reversal of the previous case; the two origins must differ
index 0xffffffff -- the maximum, and the value a null outpoint carries
index 258 = 0x00000102, so a big-endian encoding of n gives a different origin
